title: Personal Loans Collections Standard: Days Past Due, Reporting and Charge-Off
content:
## Standard

Days past due on a Personal Loans loan are counted from the next due date (the oldest unpaid due date) to today. Delinquency is reported to the credit bureaus once a loan reaches the grade's delinquency reporting days past due. A loan is charged off once the current date is at least the charge-off days past due after the oldest unpaid due date. Days past due are counted in calendar days starting the day after the oldest unpaid due date.

A loan in an active hardship plan whose plan installments are paid is not charged off, because plan installments keep the loan's due dates current under the hardship rules. Interest stops accruing on charge-off; unpaid fees remain owed. A charged-off loan becomes settled only when a Charged-Off Settlement Plan on it is completed, and paid off when the full charged-off balance is recovered.

Days past due are 0 while the next due date is today or later.

## Counting (120-day charge-off, hypothetical dates, non-leap year)

| Oldest unpaid due date | Today | Days past due | Charged off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 January | 31 January | 30 | no; reported to the bureaus |
| 1 January | 30 April | 119 | no |
| 1 January | 1 May | 120 | yes |

## After charge-off

| Event on a charged-off loan | Result |
|---|---|
| Charged-Off Settlement Plan completed for less than the full balance | settled |
| full charged-off balance recovered | paid off |
